title: Confocal imaging from biphoton correlations
summary: Confocal microscopy provides optical sectioning for three-dimensional imaging but conventionally relies on point-by-point scanning and physical pinholes, limiting imaging speed. Here, we demonstrate that confocal sectioning can instead arise directly from quantum measurement, using spatial correlations in entangled biphoton states. Spatially resolved coincidence measurements in a widefield imaging system suppress contributions from out-of-focus planes, producing optical sectioning in parallel across the whole field of view without physical pinholes or mechanical scanning.
